title: Growth hormone and IGF-1
what: This blood test checks growth hormone and a substance it helps the body make. The second one gives a better idea of your average growth hormone level.
why: In children, if a child is growing more slowly than other kids. In adults, if hands, feet, or facial features get bigger, and for pituitary gland conditions.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you or your child get growth hormone shots
If you have diabetes or problems with nutrition
If you were recently ill or lost a lot of weight

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Blood is usually taken in the morning on an empty stomach: 8 to 12 hours without food. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Rest
prepare.text: No hard workouts the day before. Sit quietly before the draw. Growth hormone changes with exercise and stress.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything needs to change before the test.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Tell your child there will be a quick prick. Bring water and a snack for afterward.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Your child's height records over the years, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
A child may get scared. Sit close and hold their hand
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Sometimes the doctor needs extra tests with a medicine. That is a separate test
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.q: Why is growth hormone alone not enough?
faq.a: It is released in bursts, so one sample says little. IGF-1 is more stable, so they are checked together.

faq.q: Does a low result mean my child needs shots?
faq.a: No. An endocrinologist, a hormone doctor, decides after a full checkup.

reminders.text: Growth hormone and IGF-1 test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Water is fine. No exercise in the morning.
